english: You kneel down to examine the skeletal remains.
Goblin. Old. Very old.
Pre-Integration, perhaps.
Hello there, little guy.
(Cast Speak with Dead.)
E-"Rest well, skull."
No response.
The skull stares back. Empty.
He crouches beside you, studying the bones.
A goblin. Real old though.
Before my time. Before my parents' time, even.
Wonder what he was doing down here.
Or she.
Statistically, this should be a male.
They are more likely to put themselves in dungeon delving danger.
Statistics speak of nothing of reality.
Wait for confirmation, before you gender the dead.
You finish casting the spell, and the skull begins to rattle.
The jaw twitches. Opens. Closes.
A dry, rasping breath that isn't breath.
It is ready.
The voice is thin. Fragile. Like wind through dead leaves.
Can you speak Diminorian?
He shrugs. "Don't look at me. That's the old tongue."
A pause. The skull tilts, slightly.
Tuigim thú... teanga an fhorghabhálaí...
I speak... the tongue of the... slayer.
The word drips with old bitterness.
What is your name?
How did you die?
What were you doing down here?
What do you think of Urth?
What happened to your people?
Tadhg Ó Scáthláin.
In your tongue... Shadow's Son.
A name from before the Integration.
When goblins still had their own names.
The skull is silent for a moment.
I am not... dead.
I am resting. Before the final stretch.
He doesn't know.
Ag teitheadh.
Escaping.
The city above. The temples. The... destruction.
He spits the last word. Or tries to. No spit left.
They take our names. Our tongue. Our gods.
I refuse to go to their schools.
I will flee into the Undercoast Path.
Urth.
The name comes out like a curse.
Your walking god. Your conqueror.
He crushed us beneath his heel and called it mercy.
I do not think of him. I refuse to.
Old hatred. Centuries old.
Still burning.
An cosán...
Yes. I knew the way.
Past the hall of fire. The trapped corridor.
There is a hidden door. In the wall beyond.
Press the third stone from the floor. On the left side.
It opens to the deep paths.
The Undercoast Path.
A network of tunnels beneath the Coast. Largely unmapped.
The skull is still. Very still.
An t-ár mór.
The great slaughter.
Your histories do not speak of it. But we remember.
We always remember.
Four questions remaining.
That's two. Three more questions.
Three asked. Two more.
One question remaining.
The skull's jaw stiffens. The false life fades.
Snell stands beside you with a dark expression.
Yeah. That's about what I imagined.
E-(Leave.)
That opinion is still regular among goblins, for your information.
Might be good to keep in mind.
Maybe. Hard not to.
But it's not important right now.
What's important is that Undercoast Path he mentioned. Let's go check it out.
